text:
sara: Heads up 1: async Python SDK retries are dropping user-supplied Idempotency-Key on retry, resulting in duplicate creates in prod. Minimal repro below.

sara: repro:
```py
await client.post('/v1/outputs', json={'prompt':'hi'}, headers={'Idempotency-Key': key})
```

sara: logs show attempt=1 had header, attempt=2 did not. Server created two resources.

kevin_m: That smells like the async transport recreating request without copying headers. Is this only async?

sara: Yes, sync path still preserves. I traced to async_transport._prepare_request.

jordan: Async codepath historically serializes the body and re-builds headers; forgot to carry user headers sometimes.

elyse: Quick mitigation: we can deep-copy headers into each retry attempt. Longer-term: auto-gen Idempotency-Key for non-idempotent endpoints (opt-in).

mika: Please file an issue and add a unit test simulating 502 then 200 asserting server saw Idempotency-Key on retries.

sara: Filed #3320 and attached logs + small repro.

ci-bot: CI failure on PR 8499 1 test_async_retries_preserve_headers failed. https://ci.redwood.internal/8499

kevin_m: I'll take PR. Plan: change _prepare_request to use dict(user_headers or {}) so mapping types are preserved, add async unit test, and update typing to Mapping[str, str] across public API.

jordan: Good call on Mapping; accept frozen/mapping types. Also add case-insensitive header test.

kevin_m: Patch ready, tests added. Leaving follow-up RFC to propose client option auto_idempotency=False by default.

sara: Verified fix locally; no dupes on repro. Thanks!

mika: Backport to v1 once merged, this is customer-impacting. Marking p1. :thumbsup:
